hints: Focus on what HCN does to a carbonyl, it adds across the C=O to make a cyanohydrin with a new C(OH)(CN) group.
Check butanal first, its product carbon is attached to H, OH, CN and a propyl group, so count how many different groups that is.
Now apply the same four-different-groups test to the two ketones, where the carbonyl carbon starts with two different alkyl groups.
walkthrough:
**Recall the cyanohydrin reaction**

Aldehydes and ketones undergo nucleophilic addition with HCN to form hydroxynitriles. The C=O becomes C(OH)(CN).

$$\text{RCHO + HCN} \rightarrow \text{RCH(OH)CN}$$
$$\text{RR'C=O + HCN} \rightarrow \text{RR'C(OH)CN}$$

**Test 1, butanal**

Butanal is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$. Its product is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CN}$.

The new carbon has four groups: H, OH, CN and $\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. All four are different, so it is a chiral centre. So 1 is correct.

**Test 2, butanone and 3, pentan-2-one**

Butanone is $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$. Its product is $\text{CH}_3\text{C(OH)(CN)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$.

The new carbon has OH, CN, $\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. Methyl and ethyl are different, so all four are different and it is chiral.

Pentan-2-one is $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. Its product is $\text{CH}_3\text{C(OH)(CN)CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. The new carbon has OH, CN, $\text{CH}_3$ and propyl, again four different groups, so it is chiral. So 2 and 3 are correct.

**Conclude the combination**

Since 1, 2 and 3 all give a product with four different groups on the former carbonyl carbon, all three produce a molecule containing a chiral centre.

options.A: Correct, because 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. Each cyanohydrin has a carbon bonded to four different groups, so each contains a new chiral centre.
options.B: Incorrect. This would mean only 1 and 2 work. Students choose this if they think pentan-2-one is too similar to butanone to be chiral, but methyl versus propyl are still different groups, so 3 is also chiral.
options.C: Incorrect. This would mean only 2 and 3 work. Students choose this if they think aldehydes cannot form chiral cyanohydrins because they contain H, but H counts as a different group from OH, CN and propyl, so 1 is chiral too.
options.D: Incorrect. This would mean only 1 works. Students choose this if they think ketones give two identical alkyl groups, but butanone has methyl and ethyl, and pentan-2-one has methyl and propyl, so both ketone products are chiral.
